title: Ind AS 20 "Accounting for Government Grants and Disclosure of Government Assistance"
outcomes: Apply the recognition conditions for government grants.
Recognise grants in profit or loss using the income approach.
Present grants related to assets and income.
Account for below-market loans, non-monetary grants and repayments.

meta.exam_tip: Ask "which cost does this grant pay for?" — that decides when it hits profit.

concepts.title: Grants, assistance and recognition conditions
body: Government grants are resources handed over by government to a business because it has met, or will meet, conditions linked to how it operates. Government assistance is wider: action to give an economic benefit to a qualifying entity, including help that cannot reasonably be valued (free technical advice) — only disclosed.

A grant, including a non-monetary grant at fair value, is booked only once it is reasonably assured both that the conditions will be met and that the money (or asset) will actually arrive. Receiving a grant is not itself proof of compliance.

A forgivable loan is treated as a grant when there is reasonable assurance the entity will meet the terms for forgiveness. Grants received as compensation for past losses or immediate financial support with no future costs are recognised in profit or loss when receivable.
concepts.analogy: Two assurances — comply and receive — must both exist before recognition.
concepts.work: A subsidy promised for setting up in a backward area is recognised once compliance is reasonably assured.

concepts.title: Income approach and matching
body: Ind AS 20 uses the income approach: grants reach profit or loss in a systematic pattern, across the same periods that bear the costs the grant is meant to cover. Crediting grants directly to equity is not allowed.

Grants for depreciable assets are recognised over the periods and in proportion to depreciation. Grants for non-depreciable assets (land) that require fulfilment of obligations are recognised over the periods bearing those costs (e.g. building a factory on it).
A grant may come with a package of conditions; the conditions creating the costs determine the recognition pattern.
concepts.analogy: Match the grant with the cost it pays for.
concepts.work: A grant for a 10-year asset is spread over 10 years.

concepts.title: Presenting asset and income grants
body: Asset-related grants (non-monetary ones included, at fair value) appear in the balance sheet either as deferred income, or by deducting the grant from the asset's carrying amount (reduced depreciation).
Income-related grants appear within profit or loss, either separately or under "other income", or deducted in reporting the related expense.
Cash flow statements show the grant and asset purchase as separate items regardless of balance sheet presentation.
concepts.analogy: Two presentation choices each for asset and income grants; both give the same profit.
concepts.work: A wage subsidy may be shown as other income or netted against salaries.

concepts.title: Below-market loans, non-monetary grants and repayment
body: The benefit of a government loan below market rate is treated as a grant: the loan is recognised and measured under Ind AS 109 at fair value, and the difference from proceeds is the grant, accounted for under Ind AS 20.
A non-monetary grant (land, other resources) is measured at fair value.

A grant becoming repayable is a change in estimate. Repayment of an income-related grant is applied first against any unamortised deferred credit, with the excess expensed. For an asset grant, the carrying amount is increased (or deferred income reduced); cumulative extra depreciation that would have been charged without the grant is recognised immediately in profit or loss.
concepts.analogy: Cheap loans hide a grant; repayment is a prospective change in estimate.
concepts.work: Land received free from government is booked at fair value with deferred income.

jobs.title: Grant compliance tracker
jobs.situation: A new plant received capital subsidy, power subsidy and an interest-free loan.
steps: Confirm reasonable assurance for each grant.
Choose presentation for the capital subsidy.
Measure the loan at fair value.
jobs.takeaway: Every grant needs a recognition basis and a compliance check.

mcqs.q: Besides reasonable assurance of meeting the conditions, recognising a grant needs reasonable assurance that:
mcqs.explain: Both assurances are needed. In practice: receipt alone is not enough.

mcqs.q: Crediting a capital grant directly to shareholders' equity is:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 20 follows the income approach. In practice: use deferred income.

mcqs.q: A grant for a depreciable asset is recognised in profit or loss:
mcqs.explain: Matching with related costs. In practice: deferred income released yearly.

mcqs.q: The benefit of a below-market government loan is measured as:
options: Proceeds minus fair value under Ind AS 109
mcqs.explain: It is treated as a grant. In practice: use market rate to discount.
mcqs.topic: Below-market loans, non-monetary grants and repayment

mcqs.explain: Ind AS 20 requires fair value. In practice: land received free.
mcqs.topic: Below-market loans, non-monetary grants and repayment

mcqs.q: Repayment of a grant is accounted for as:
mcqs.explain: Prospective treatment. In practice: catch-up depreciation for asset grants.
mcqs.topic: Below-market loans, non-monetary grants and repayment

mcqs.q: Free technical advice from government that cannot be valued is:
mcqs.explain: Only disclosure is required. In practice: describe nature and extent.

mcqs.q: Grants related to assets may be presented as:
options: Deferred income or a deduction from the asset
mcqs.explain: Two choices. In practice: cash flows show gross.

summary: Recognise when compliance and receipt are reasonably assured.
Income approach; no direct credit to equity.
Asset grants: deferred income or deduct from asset.
Below-market loans: grant = proceeds − fair value.
traps: Recognising the grant when cash arrives.

viva.q: What are the recognition conditions for a grant?
viva.model: Reasonable assurance that the entity will meet the attached conditions and that the grant will be received.

viva.q: Why does Ind AS 20 use the income approach?
viva.model: Because grants come from a source other than shareholders and are earned by meeting obligations, so they should be matched with related costs in profit or loss.

viva.q: How are grants related to income presented?
viva.model: Either as separate or other income in profit or loss, or deducted from the related expense.

viva.q: How is repayment of an asset-related grant treated?
viva.model: The asset is increased or deferred income reduced, and the cumulative additional depreciation is charged to profit or loss immediately.

points.pt: Increase asset or reduce deferred income

viva.q: How is a forgivable loan treated?
viva.model: As a grant once there is reasonable assurance the entity will meet the terms for forgiveness.

cases.title: Delta Pharma Ltd.
cases.case: Delta Pharma Ltd. receives: (1) land worth ₹50 lakh free from the state, on condition it builds a plant within 2 years (plant life 20 years); (2) ₹12 lakh to cover salaries of trainees in the current year; (3) ₹8 lakh as compensation for flood losses of the previous year.

mcqs.q: The land is recognised at (₹ lakh):
mcqs.explain: Non-monetary grants at fair value. In practice: deferred income.
mcqs.topic: Below-market loans, non-monetary grants and repayment

mcqs.q: The land grant is released to profit or loss:
options: Over the life of the plant built on it
mcqs.explain: Costs of meeting obligations — plant depreciation — determine the pattern. In practice: 20 years.

mcqs.q: The trainee salary grant is recognised in:
mcqs.explain: Matched with the salary cost. In practice: show as other income or reduce expense.

mcqs.q: Compensation for past flood losses is recognised:
options: In profit or loss when receivable
mcqs.explain: No future costs to match. In practice: disclose if material.
